source: murder mystery game in a mansion

image_prompt.text: Wardrobes, curtained alcoves and furniture gaps set into the mansion walls where players break the murderer sightline and hide, at least 4 studs on the entry axis
Large doors set into the outer wall of the mansion acting as the round-win trigger
The mansion itself - rooms, halls and corridors the players move around inside

layout_placement.text: Separated start points so the murderer and the other players do not begin on top of each other
The exit that ends the round when reached

notes: Classified as Survival 1 vs All rather than Party and Casual because the pressure is a pursuing threat with asymmetric roles, which is the boundary rule in the Survival notes.

The mansion is the entire map, not a building inside a larger map. building-interior was used because it is the only way a genre file can say interior, and it charges P3 for an outside-to-inside transition that this build may not have; the no-genre interior-only axis would have cost nothing.
Preset caveat: 1 vs All carries an escape gate. Many murder-mystery games end on the murderer being caught rather than on an exit, but the prompt does not say either way, so the gate was kept.

open_questions.ask: Should the mansion read as grand and well-lit, or dim and gothic?
How does a round end - the murderer is caught, everyone is killed, or survivors escape through a door?

coverage_missing.ask: How does a round end, and is there a sheriff or detective role as well as a murderer?
Bright and elegant, or dim and gothic?
How big is the mansion - a handful of rooms, or a sprawling estate with grounds?
Is play entirely inside the mansion, or are the grounds and gardens in play too?

answers.ask: Should the mansion read as grand and well-lit, or dim and gothic?
answers.answer: Make it dim and gothic to fit the murder mystery mansion setting.

answers.ask: How does a round end - the murderer is caught, everyone is killed, or survivors escape through a door?
answers.answer: A round ends when the murderer is caught, or when the murderer eliminates all other players.
